chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sayaba, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: 'Al-Sawiq was revealed by the Revelation from the sky.'

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: A traditional food made from flour, often mixed with water or milk, considered blessed.
key_terms.بِالْوَحْيِ: By means of divine revelation or inspiration.
key_terms.مِنَ السَّمَاءِ: From the sky, indicating a celestial or divine origin.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Al-Sawiq in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that Al-Sawiq (a simple flour-based dish) was 'sent down' via revelation, emphasizing its status as a blessed, divinely sanctioned sustenance rather than merely a culinary invention. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that humble foods can carry spiritual merit and physical benefits when consumed with gratitude, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of simplicity and moderation in diet.

en.hubeali:
From him, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Sayaba, from Jundab Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘But rather, Al-Suweyq was Revealed by the Revelation from the sky’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from A number of our people have narrated from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Sayabah from Jundab ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying,
sawiq was made by the instruction from the heavens.’”
